concepts.description: The SRanger system is a small ground robot that travels in a straight line and turns in place when it detects an obstacle.
A single infrared (IR) distance sensor mounted facing forward.
A reactive controller that uses the IR-driven obstacle event and emits motor commands as advisory events.
An event that the controller receives or emits.
An Actuator interface that records the last motor command.
A single state machine that selects transitions based on the input event, the IR distance, and the elapsed time in the current mode.
A state variable, notably a clock-reset timestamp for the timed Turning → Moving transition.
The current operating mode used by the state machine to select transitions.
A real-valued fixed configuration constant used by the SRanger controller.
An input event received by the SRanger controller from three sources.
An output event emitted by the SRanger controller.
A function provided by the Sensor.

instances.description: IR-driven obstacle event used as the controller's only sensor input.
System-level endTask event available to halt the controller.
Initial mode in which the robot drives forward at the configured linear velocity.
Mode in which the robot rotates in place at the configured angular velocity.
Terminal mode entered when the operator issues endTask.
Default 1.0 m/s; linear velocity command when Moving.
Default 2.0 rad/s; angular velocity command when Turning.
Default 0.5 metres; IR-distance threshold for the obstacle-detection condition.
Default 2.0 seconds; time the controller remains in Turning before returning to Moving.
Delivered each control cycle by the system framework.
Single output event carrying linear and angular velocity to the differential-drive layer.
Returns the latest IR distance reading in metres, non-negative; returns a large default value when no reading is available.
Records when the controller most recently entered the Turning state; set on the Moving → Turning transition and used for the autonomous Turning → Moving transition.
